instruction: Insert a new provision to read as follows and renumber succeeding provisions accordingly: QUICK RESPONSE FUND. THE AMOUNT OF SIX HUNDRED MILLION PESOS (P600,000,000) APPROPRIATED HEREIN FOR THE QUICK RESPONSE FUND (QRF) SHALL SERVE AS A STAND-BY FUND TO BE USED FOR: (I) PROVISION OF VARIOUS PRODUCTION INPUTS, INCLUDING SEEDS, PLANTING MATERIALS, FEEDS, AND OTHER NECESSARY FARM INPUTS, FOR AGRARIAN REFORM BENEFICIARIES (ARBS) AND THEIR ORGANIZATIONS; (II) REPAIR OF PRODUCTION AND POST-PRODUCTION FACILITIES, SMALL-SCALE IRRIGATION SYSTEMS, EQUIPMENT, AND MACHINERY USED BY ARBS AND THEIR ORGANIZATIONS; (III) PROVISION OF OTHER ASSISTANCE, INCLUDING CASH AND LIVELIHOOD RECOVERY ASSISTANCE, TO ARBS AFFECTED BY NATURAL OR HUMAN-INDUCED CALAMITIES, EPIDEMICS, CRISES, AND CATASTROPHES; AND (IV) PROVISION OF NECESSARY TOOLS, SUPPLIES, WATER ACCESS, AND IRRIGATION SUPPORT DIRECTLY USED TO MITIGATE THE EFFECTS OF AN ONGOING DISASTER, INCLUDING EL NIÑO-INDUCED DROUGHT, SUBJECT TO GUIDELINES ISSUED BY THE DAR, IN COORDINATION WITH THE DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND OTHER CONCERNED AGENCIES, IN ORDER THAT THE SITUATION AND LIVING CONDITIONS OF AFFECTED ARBS AND THEIR COMMUNITIES MAY BE NORMALIZED AS QUICKLY AS POSSIBLE. IN NO CASE SHALL THE QRF BE USED FOR PRE-DISASTER ACTIVITIES, SUCH AS CONDUCT OF TRAINING, INSURANCE OF ASSETS, AND PUBLIC INFORMATION AND EDUCATION INITIATIVES, OR ANY OTHER PURPOSE NOT AUTHORIZED IN THIS PROVISION.

The amended paragraph will now read as follows: 8. Quick Response Fund. The amount of TWO BILLION PESOS (P2,000,000,000) appropriated herein for the Quick Response Fund (QRF) shall serve as a stand-by fund to be used for: (i) provision of various production inputs for crops, livestock, and poultry; (ii) repair of production, post- production facilities, small-scale irrigation systems, equipment, and machinery; (iii) provision of other assistance in the form of cash for culled live animals, and fuel assistance to farmers, subject to guidelines issued by the DA; (iv) provision of necessary tools and supplies directly used to mitigate the effects of an ongoing disaster; AND (V) PROVISION OF NECESSARY ASSISTANCE TO FARMERS AND AFFECTED COMMUNITIES TO ADDRESS THE IMPACTS OF EL NIÑO-INDUCED DROUGHT, INCLUDING WATER ACCESS, IRRIGATION SUPPORT, AND THE PROVISION OF SEEDS, FEEDS, AND OTHER ESSENTIAL AGRICULTURAL INPUTS, in order that the situation and living conditions of people in communities or areas affected by natural or human-induced calamities, epidemics, crises and catastrophes, which occurred in the last quarter of the immediately preceding year and those occurring during the current year may be normalized as quickly as possible. The amended paragraph will now read as follows: 11. Farm-to-Market Road Projects. The amount of SIXTEEN BILLION PESOS (P16,000,000,000) appropriated herein for Farm-to-Market Road (FMR) projects shall be used for the construction, improvement, rehabilitation, and repair of FMRs in accordance with the National FMR Network Plan (2023-2028). For this purpose, the DA through its Bureau of Agriculture and Fisheries Engineering (BAFE) and Regional Field Units (RFUs) shall undertake the planning and implementation of the program and may enter into a MOA with the DPWH, qualified LGUs or through Public Private Partnerships. The DA shall ensure that: (i) the FMR network plan shall include the scope of work, estimated length in kilometers, and specific location for each of the FMR projects, as well as a list of priority FMR projects, which must lead to arterial or secondary roads and key production areas; (ii) the detailed engineering design and program of works have passed technical review; (iii) prior to the procurement of any FMR project, the approved budget for the contract is subjected to cost validation by the DA-BAFE, taking into account prevailing market prices, standard unit costs, and site-specific conditions; and (iv) the FMRs implemented are properly geo-tagged. xxx

instruction: Insert a new provision to read as follows and renumber succeeding provisions accordingly: CROP, LIVESTOCK, AND AQUACULTURE DIVERSIFICATION. THE DA SHALL PROMOTE DIVERSIFICATION AND ROTATION OF CROPS, LIVESTOCK, AND AQUACULTURE SPECIES TO ENSURE LOCAL ADAPTABILITY, AND MITIGATE SPECIES-SPECIFIC RISKS ARISING FROM CLIMATE CHANGE. FURTHER, THE DA SHALL SUPPORT CLIMATE-RESILIENT AND NUTRIENT-DENSE FOOD SYSTEMS, ESPECIALLY IN URBAN AREAS, USING BEST PRACTICES AND APPROPRIATE TECHNOLOGIES, INCLUDING NATURE- BASED SOLUTIONS, WHENEVER POSSIBLE, TO REDUCE, WITHSTAND, AND RECOVER FROM THE IMPACTS OF CLIMATE CHANGE. THE DA SHALL LIKEWISE ENCOURAGE AGRO-TOURISM AND AGRI-BUSINESS INVESTMENTS ALONG AGRI INDUSTRIAL BUSINESS CORRIDORS (ABCS) AND IN AGRICULTURAL COMMUNITIES TO GENERATE ADDITIONAL INCOME OPPORTUNITIES, ENHANCE LOCAL VALUE ADDITION, AND STIMULATE INCLUSIVE RURAL DEVELOPMENT.

amended_text: 7. Climate Change Information Management System. The DENR, pursuant to its mandate under the Climate Change Act, shall oversee the establishment and maintenance of a Climate Change Information Management System (CCIMS) and Network AS AN INTEGRATED INFORMATION AND DECISION-SUPPORT PLATFORM FOR CLIMATE CHANGE ADAPTATION, MITIGATION, DISASTER RISK REDUCTION, CLIMATE INVESTMENTS, AND CLIMATE- RESILIENT DEVELOPMENT. amended_text: 11. Unified River Basin and Flood Management Database. The DENR, in coordination with DPWH, shall jointly develop, maintain, and enhance a unified river basin and flood management database to support integrated, science-based, and climate- and disaster-risk-informed planning for watershed rehabilitation, river basin management, flood risk reduction, and climate-resilient development. amended_text: 1. Higher Education Development Fund. In addition to the amounts appropriated herein, the amount chargeable against the SAGF reflected in the BESF Table B.15 under the FY 2027 Proposed Expenditures shall be used for the requirements of the COMMISSION ON HIGHER EDUCATION (CHED), sourced from the following in accordance with Section 10 of R.A. Further, the share from the proceeds from any sale, after deducting all expenses related to the sale, of portions of Metro Manila military camps by the Bases Conversion and Development Authority authorized under R.A. No. 7227, as amended, shall also be contributed to the Higher Education Development Fund (HEDF). Release of funds shall be subject to the submission of a budget request and other relevant budgetary requirements, AND in accordance with judicious fiscal programming by the National Government, as well as applicable laws, rules, and regulations. In the overall programming of the HEDF, the CHED shall ensure that the full requirements of existing scholars are considered to guarantee their continuing funding and to prioritize support TO courses or programs aligned with global innovation platforms, as well as the priorities of the government in key growth areas in the grant of research extension and scholarships, implementation and support to presidential directives, newly promulgated laws on higher education, workforce development and priority developments for tourism education and regional education tourism hubs. The CHED En Banc is authorized to use the HEDF to fund qualified new Tertiary Education Subsidy (TES) grantees, prioritizing those from low income households consistent with R.A. No. 10931, who cannot be covered by the current year's appropriations for TES. Likewise, all outstanding deficiencies for State Universities and Colleges' (SUCs) Free Higher Education (FHE) may be charged against their respective internally generated funds. In case of insufficiency thereof, the same shall be charged against the HEDF, subject to accounting and auditing rules and regulations.

instruction: Delete Special Provision No. 6 and replace with a new provision to read as follows: 6. MODIFICATION OF IRRIGATION PROJECT LIST. NO CHANGE OR MODIFICATION TO THE APPROVED LIST OF IRRIGATION PROJECTS SHALL BE ALLOWED EXCEPT WHEN SUPPORTED BY CLEAR, VERIFIABLE, AND SCIENTIFICALLY ESTABLISHED GROUNDS. THESE GROUNDS ARE SPECIFICALLY LIMITED TO: (i) HYDROGEOLOGICAL FAILURE EVIDENCED BY FAILED PUMP TESTS DUE TO INSUFFICIENT GROUNDWATER RECHARGE AND SHIFT IN RIVER COURSE VALIDATED THROUGH HYDROGEOLOGICAL SURVEY RESULTS; (ii) REALIGNMENT OF CANALS WHERE ORIGINAL ALIGNMENTS ARE NO LONGER VIABLE DUE TO HIGH SILTATION, EROSION, LANDSLIDE-PRONE SLOPES, OR UNSAFE SOIL BEARING CAPACITY, AND UNSTABLE SUBSURFACE CONDITIONS DURING WELL DEVELOPMENT; (iii) PHYSICAL INACCESSIBILITY ESTABLISHED BY CERTIFIED DOCUMENTATION FROM RELEVANT GOVERNMENT AUTHORITIES IN CASES OF PERMANENT SITE INACCESSIBILITY, SUCH AS LANDSLIDE, FLOODING, OR A LEGALLY UNRESOLVED RIGHT-OF-WAY; OR (iv) RECONSTRUCTION OF DAMAGED IRRIGATION STRUCTURES DUE TO TYPHOONS, FLOODS, AND ACTS OF MAN, SUCH AS BUT NOT LIMITED TO QUARRYING. PROVIDED, THAT ANY MODIFICATION SHALL REQUIRE JOINT CERTIFICATION BY THE NIA REGIONAL MANAGER AND A LICENSED GEOLOGIST OR GEOTECHNICAL/CIVIL ENGINEER WHO IS INDEPENDENT OF THE PROJECT PROPONENT, ENDORSEMENT BY THE NIA ADMINISTRATOR, AND FINAL APPROVAL BY THE NIA BOARD, AND SHALL NOT BE BASED SOLELY ON ADMINISTRATIVE OR MANAGERIAL DISCRETION: PROVIDED, FURTHER, THAT ANY RELOCATION SHALL REMAIN STRICTLY WITHIN THE SAME PROVINCE, BE LIMITED TO SITES MEETING THE SAME TECHNICAL CRITERIA, AND COMPLY FULLY WITH APPLICABLE LAWS, RULES, AND REGULATIONS.
